```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
options(width = 100)
library(sciparseR)
ex <- function(f) system.file("extdata", f, package = "sciparseR")
```

A PDF file stores glyphs and their positions, not paragraphs. sciparseR
rebuilds the reading structure from the word boxes that pdftools reports.
This article explains each step and shows it on the bundled fixtures,
each of which comes with a ground truth file used by the tests.

## From words to lines

Words are grouped into lines by vertical overlap, and a line is split into
segments where the horizontal gap is larger than `segment_gap` times the
line height. Small raised words become superscripts (footnote markers,
citation numbers).

```{r}
doc <- sc_parse(ex("single_column.pdf"))
head(doc$lines[, c("line_id", "page", "y0", "font_size", "text")], 5)
head(doc$spans[doc$spans$superscript, c("text", "line_id")])
```

## Columns and reading order

The default reading order is a recursive XY-cut: a page region is split at
the widest vertical whitespace gutter (a column break) or horizontal gap,
and the parts are read top to bottom, left to right. Lines that cross a
gutter, such as a full width title or abstract, are kept together.

```{r}
two <- sc_parse(ex("two_column.pdf"))
sc_pages(two)[, c("page", "n_columns")]
p <- sc_blocks(two, type = c("heading", "paragraph"))
p[, c("reading_order", "column", "type")][1:8, ]
substr(p$text[1:6], 1, 60)
```

The `broken_order.pdf` fixture writes its text in a scrambled order inside
the file. The stream order (the order in the file) is wrong; the
geometric order is right:

```{r}
geo <- sc_parse(ex("broken_order.pdf"))
str <- sc_parse(ex("broken_order.pdf"), config = sc_config(reading_order = "stream"))
truth <- sub("\\.pdf$", ".truth.json", ex("broken_order.pdf"))
rbind(xycut = sc_evaluate(geo, truth)$value[1:3], stream = sc_evaluate(str, truth)$value[1:3])
```

## Headers, footers and page numbers

Text that repeats in the top or bottom band of several pages
(`header_band`) is a running header or footer; a lone number there is a
page number. These blocks keep their type, so they are available, but
`sc_text()` leaves them out.

```{r}
doc$blocks[doc$blocks$type %in% c("header", "footer", "page_number"), c("page", "type", "text")]
```

## Hyphenation

A word broken at a line end ("random-" / "ized") is rejoined only when the
joined word appears elsewhere in the document, or when the second part
starts in lower case and the joined form is a plausible word. Real
hyphenated compounds stay as they are.

```{r}
grepl("randomized", sc_text(doc))
grepl("random- ized", sc_text(doc), fixed = TRUE)
```

## Paragraphs across pages

A paragraph that continues on the next page is linked rather than merged,
so each block keeps its own page and box. `sc_text()` joins them with a
space.

```{r}
cont <- doc$blocks[!is.na(doc$blocks$continues), c("block_id", "page", "continues")]
cont
```

## Rotated pages

Pages with a `/Rotate` entry are detected and their words are mapped to
the upright page:

```{r}
rot <- sc_parse(ex("rotated.pdf"))
sc_pages(rot)[, c("page", "rotation", "rotation_status", "width", "height")]
substr(sc_text(rot), 1, 120)
```

## Image-only pages

A page with ink but no text layer is flagged, never silently empty. See
`vignette("ocr-models-grobid")` for the optional OCR step.

```{r}
scan <- sc_parse(ex("scanned.pdf"))
sc_pages(scan)[, c("page", "has_text_layer", "image_only", "ocr_status", "ink_ratio")]
```

## Unicode

Greek letters, mathematical operators and accented names are kept as
Unicode and normalized to NFC:

```{r}
cat(sc_text(sc_parse(ex("unicode.pdf"))))
```

## Settings

All thresholds live in `sc_config()`. The defaults work for typical
journal layouts; `column_gap` and `segment_gap` are the first to adjust
for unusual layouts. Switching `render = FALSE` skips page rendering,
which is faster but disables ruling line detection for tables and figure
regions.

```{r}
sc_config(column_gap = 1.5, render = FALSE)
```
